intro: Thailand is hot and humid most of the year, so you can pack light — but a few items are painful to forget, from modest temple wear to sunscreen and rainy-season gear. Here is the checklist.

blocks.html: Short answer: Pack light, breathable clothes for the heat and humidity, add a modest shoulder- and knee-covering outfit for temples, sunscreen, a foldable umbrella/rain jacket, secure sandals and a small medical kit. Thai power is 220V with plug types A/B/C — most European/US devices fit, but check the voltage first.

items: A modest outfit covering shoulders and knees for temples/palaces
Sunscreen (reef-safe for the sea) + hat + sunglasses
Foldable umbrella or rain jacket, especially in the rainy season
Secure sandals or water shoes — comfy to walk and rain-friendly
Basic meds: anti-diarrheal, antihistamine, insect repellent, plasters, personal prescriptions
Adapter/power bank and a waterproof phone pouch

blocks.title: Do not over-pack
blocks.html: Clothes, toiletries and basic medicines are cheap and easy to buy across Thailand. Pack only what you need and top up locally — and leave room for souvenirs.

faq.q: What should I wear in Thailand?
faq.a: Mostly light, breathable clothing for the heat and humidity, but bring a modest outfit covering shoulders and knees for temples and palaces. Beachwear is fine at the beach, but dress respectfully in towns and sacred sites.

faq.q: What power plugs does Thailand use?
faq.a: Thailand uses 220V with plug types A/B/C; most sockets accept both round and flat pins. UK three-square-pin devices need an adapter, and 110V-only devices need a voltage converter.

faq.q: Should I bring my own medicine?
faq.a: Bring enough of your personal prescriptions and keep the prescription itself. Basic items like anti-diarrheal or insect repellent are easy to buy at pharmacies and convenience stores across Thailand.

quickAnswerHtml: Pack light, breathable clothes for the heat and humidity, bring a modest outfit covering shoulders and knees for temples, and don't forget sunscreen, an umbrella, and basic meds. Thailand uses 220V with plug types A/B/C — most European and US devices fit directly, but always check the voltage first.
